newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech IPB tender rules coming soon-FinMin.
newsitem.headline: Czech IPB tender rules coming soon-FinMin.

text.p: Conditions for a tender to sell the state's roughly one-third holding in the fourth largest Czech bank, IPB a.s., will be announced by the end of January, Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik said on Tuesday.
"The conditions of the tender will be stated now, in a short time. Definitely by the end of January," he told Reuters after a news conference on the 1996 state budget.

A special committee has been formed at the Finance Ministry to prepare the sale, which is expected to be geared toward choosing a strong foreign partner, and an adviser for the tender should be selected soon, he said.
"We have gathered the offers and it is in the process of evaluation now. The adviser will be chosen by mid January," the minister said.

A key economic aide to Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, Martin Kocourek, said in November that Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) was seeking to be the arranger for the IPB selloff. Other firms seeking the mandate, if any, have not been revealed.
The government holds a 31.5 percent stake in IPB through its National Property Fund (NPF), and another roughly six percent through the postal service Ceska Posta.
The exact amount of shares to be offered in the tender has not been released.

NPF chairman Roman Ceska, who does not have a seat in the cabinet which must ultimately approve the sale, said in the Czech daily Pravo on Monday that Japanese investment bank Nomura has the "best chance" to win the tender.
He also said however that he hoped the selection process would be transparent.
The tender should take about six months to complete, he said.

Apart from Nomura, the Dutch concerns ING Groep NV and ABN AMRO AAH.HS have also been touted by Czech media as parties interested in taking a stake in IPB, although both have refused to comment on the matter.
